No — `var(--mantine-playerNameMinWidthSingleLine)` won't resolve to anything. Mantine's `MantineProvider` only auto-generates CSS variables for a fixed set of theme branches (`colors`, `spacing`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `shadows`, `radius`, `fontWeights`, `breakpoints`, `headings`) via its `defaultCssVariablesResolver`. I checked that function directly (`node_modules/@mantine/core/esm/core/MantineProvider/MantineCssVariables/default-css-variables-resolver.mjs`) — it never touches `theme.other` at all, and this project's `MantineProvider` in `src/app/layout.tsx` doesn't pass a custom `cssVariablesResolver` either. So that custom property is never defined; `var()` referencing an undefined custom property with no fallback makes the whole `min-width` declaration invalid at computed-value time, and it silently falls back to `auto` — not a loud failure, just wrong-looking layout.

Two ways to actually fix `PlayerLink.tsx`:

**A. Define the CSS variables yourself** — add a `cssVariablesResolver` to `MantineProvider` in `layout.tsx` that spreads `defaultCssVariablesResolver(theme)` and adds your own (kebab-case, matching Mantine's naming convention) entries, e.g. `--player-name-min-width-single-line: theme.other.playerNameMinWidthSingleLine`. More plumbing, only worth it if you actually need these in a `.css`/CSS Module file outside of JSX.

**B. Skip CSS variables — import the `theme` object directly.** `theme.ts` exports a plain object (no React/context involved), so it's safe to import in a Server Component:

That's a reasonable call for this project, and it has a concrete upside beyond just simplicity: it would categorically eliminate the Mantine dot-notation SSR bug documented in `CLAUDE.md` (the one that bit `PlayerInfo`, `PlayerResults`, `PlayerPositions`, `PlayerArse`) — that bug only triggers when a *Server* Component touches a dot-notation subcomponent of a `'use client'` export, so if every presentation component is itself `'use client'`, the whole bug class goes away for future code, no more "always use the standalone named subcomponent" workaround needed.

I checked whether it'd actually be safe: none of the 28 currently-server presentational components are `async` or import `'server-only'`, so none of them are secretly doing data-layer work that would break by going client — the policy matches what's actually there today.

The only honest tradeoff: you'd be giving up the option to ever get server-rendering/zero-JS benefits for presentational subtrees, but per the last question, that's not worth anything at this project's scale anyway. 57	## Architecture & Layers
58	
59	- **Pages:** `src/app/footy/**` — Next.js App Router feature pages
60	- **API routes:** `src/app/api/**` — Next.js route handlers; importable via `api/*` alias
61	- **Server actions:** `src/actions/` — thin `"use server"` wrappers: auth guard + call core + revalidate + broadcast; mutations only; injected into components as required props
62	- **Action cores:** `src/lib/core/` — pure business logic called by server actions; injectable deps for testing; no Next.js boundary concerns
63	- **Services:** `src/services/` — all Prisma queries live here exclusively, one service per model
64	- **Library:** `src/lib/` — utilities, auth, config, email, Azure, dates, URLs, observability
65	- **Types:** `src/types/` — custom TypeScript types and Zod schema extensions
66	
67	**Domain ontology:** [`docs/ontology.yaml`](docs/ontology.yaml) — the meaning layer on top of `prisma/schema.prisma`: what each entity represents, how they relate, controlled vocabularies, business workflows (invitations, picker, results, money), and invariants the code enforces that the schema doesn't. Consult it before making non-trivial changes to domain logic (game days, outcomes, picker, ratings, tables, transactions) — read `prisma/schema.prisma` for structure and this file for meaning. While changes to the ontology are possible they are likley to be rare and each should be considered very carefully: the business logic and the ontology should always be kept in sync.
68	
69	**Data flow rule:** Components call services (read) or server actions (write). Never write direct Prisma calls in API routes, pages, or components — refactor into a service method. If you filter/sort service results in calling code, move that logic into the service.

71	## Key Conventions
72	
73	### Dependencies
74	
75	- `@types/d3` is listed in `devDependencies` and `ignoreDependencies` in `knip.json` even though no code imports from `d3` directly. It is kept because it pulls in all the individual `@types/d3-*` sub-packages (e.g. `@types/d3-array`, `@types/d3-axis`) as transitive npm dependencies — removing it silently removes all those type declarations.
76	
77	### Imports
78	
79	- **Always** use `@/` alias instead of `../../` relative imports
80	- Same-directory `./` imports are acceptable
81	- Always use single quotes for import paths
82	- Prepend all backend-only modules with `import 'server-only';`
83	- All imports from any `@mantine/*` package must be written multi-line, one specifier per line with a trailing comma, regardless of specifier count or line length (this applies even to a single-specifier import, e.g. `import {\n    Table,\n} from '@mantine/core';`)
84	- **Never** use Mantine's dot-notation compound components (`Table.Tr`, `Menu.Item`, `AppShell.Header`, `RichTextEditor.Bold`, etc.) — always import the standalone named subcomponent instead (`TableTr`, `MenuItem`, `AppShellHeader`, `BoldControl`, etc.) and use that directly in JSX. Reason: when a Server Component (no `'use client'`) accesses a dot-notation subcomponent of a `'use client'` package export, the property resolves to `undefined` at render time — "Element type is invalid: expected a string ... but got: undefined" — because Server Components only receive an opaque client reference for a `'use client'` export, not the real object, so its static properties aren't accessible. This is a confirmed, still-open limitation of the current Next.js/React Server Components architecture, not a bug in Mantine or this codebase (see [vercel/next.js#84961](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/84961) and the root-cause explanation in [vercel/next.js#75192](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/75192)). It bit `PlayerInfo`, `PlayerResults`, `PlayerPositions`, and `PlayerArse` in July 2026. The one exception is `RichTextEditor.Toolbar` (from `@mantine/tiptap`), which has no standalone export — leave it as dot notation, only in files that are already `'use client'`, with a comment explaining why.
85	
86	### Services Pattern
87	
88	```ts
89	import 'server-only';
90	import debug from 'debug';
91	import prisma from 'prisma/prisma';
92	import { SomeModelWhereUniqueInputObjectSchema } from 'prisma/zod/schemas';
93	import z from 'zod';
94	
95	const extendedFields = { /* extra validation */ };
96	export const SomeModelCreateStrictSchema = /* extend generated create schema */;
97	const log = debug('footy:api');
98	
99	export class SomeModelService {
100	  async get(id: number) {
101	    const where = SomeModelWhereUniqueInputObjectSchema.parse({ id });
102	    return prisma.someModel.findUnique({ where });
103	  }
104	}
105	```
106	
107	- Validate all inputs with Zod before calling Prisma (`WhereUnique`, `WhereInput`, or custom strict schema)
108	- Return `null` for "not found"; throw only on unexpected failures
109	- Use `debug('footy:api')` for logging; never `console.log`
110	- Use `lib/config.ts` for numeric thresholds instead of hardcoding
111	
112	### Prisma / Database
113	
114	- Prisma client singleton: `prisma/prisma.ts` — never instantiate another client
115	- Generated files in `prisma/generated/` and `prisma/zod/` — extend, never modify
116	- Use `z.email()` not `z.string().email()` (Zod deprecation)
117	- Never create migration files manually — use `npm run migrate`
118	- Better Auth tables (`user`, `account`, `session`, `verification`) — never modify directly via Prisma; use Better Auth APIs
119	
120	### UI & Forms
121	
122	- Use Mantine components and hooks everywhere; avoid native HTML/CSS unless no Mantine equivalent exists. Never fall back to raw `<div>`, `<section>`, `<article>` etc. just to attach ARIA attributes — use Mantine's polymorphic `component` prop (e.g. `<Card component="section">`) or `role`/`aria-*` props on the Mantine element instead
123	- Prefer Mantine style props (`bd`, `bg`, `c`, `w`, `h`, `m*`, `p*`, etc.) over the `style` prop or a CSS file/module. Only fall back to raw CSS/inline `style` when no Mantine style prop covers the property needed — CSS is the escape hatch, not the default
124	- **Always** use Mantine `useForm` for form state — never write bespoke form handlers
125	- Use `@tabler/icons-react` for icons
126	- Notifications: use Mantine `notifications` with `autoClose` from `lib/config.ts`
127	- British English for all copy and comments
128	
129	### Testing
130	
131	- Test files: `*.vitest.spec.ts(x)` placed next to the file they test — never in a `__tests__/` subdirectory
132	- Mocks: `__mocks__/` as sibling to the target code
133	- Use accessible selectors (`getByRole`, `getByLabelText`, `getByText`) over `data-testid`
134	- Do not rely on Mantine internals in tests (for example generated class names, internal DOM wrappers, or implementation-specific structure). Prefer selectors and assertions that reflect real user interactions and visible behaviour.
135	- Prefer the generic overload (`getByRole<HTMLInputElement>(…)`) over a type assertion (`as HTMLInputElement`) when narrowing query results — ESLint strips assertions but preserves generics
136	- Don't test generated Zod schemas directly — test service method behaviour and validation
137	- E2E tests: `e2e/*.spec.ts`, must be fully parallel-safe
138	
139	### Comments & JSDoc
140	
141	- Default to no comments; only add one when the WHY is non-obvious
142	- When changing a function that has a JSDoc block, update the entire block in the same edit — description, `@param`, `@returns`, `@throws`, and any other tags must all accurately reflect the new implementation
143	
144	### Live updates (revalidation & SSE)
145	
146	Every server action that mutates data must, before returning:
147	
148	1. Call `revalidatePath(…)` for every Next.js route that renders the affected data.
149	2. Call `broadcast(channel)` (or `broadcast([ch1, ch2])` for multiple) from `@/lib/events` with the relevant `FootyChannel` value(s) — so connected clients refresh without polling.
150	
151	Every page that displays data that can be mutated by a server action must render `<AutoRefresh channels={…} />` (from `@/components/AutoRefresh/AutoRefresh`) with the matching channel(s). Pass an array when the page depends on more than one channel — never render multiple `<AutoRefresh>` elements.
152	
153	`FootyChannel` values live in `src/types/FootyChannel.ts`; add a new entry there if the new feature needs its own channel.
154	
155	### Observability
156	
157	- Sentry: configured via `instrumentation.ts` / `instrumentation-client.ts` and `next.config.mjs`
158	- Preserve `tunnelRoute: '/monitoring'` and middleware matcher exclusions when editing middleware

## Summary

Found and fixed a real gap while investigating the review comment: the shared test `Wrapper` (`src/tests/components/lib/common.tsx`) rendered a bare `<MantineProvider>` without the app's actual `theme` — so `theme.other.playerNameMinWidthSingleLine`/`MultiLine` were always `undefined` in every component test, silently diverging from production (`src/app/layout.tsx` passes `theme={theme}`). That's *why* no wrap-vs-default difference was observable before — not a jsdom limitation as I'd assumed earlier in this session.

**Fixes:**
1. **`src/tests/components/lib/common.tsx`** — `Wrapper` now passes `theme={theme}` (from `@/theme`) into `MantineProvider`, matching production. Verified this doesn't break anything: full `test:components` suite (79 files, 689 tests) still passes.
2. **`PlayerLink.vitest.spec.tsx`** — replaced the routing-only `wrap` test with two assertions that actually verify the `miw` token selection: `link.style.minWidth` equals `theme.other?.playerNameMinWidthSingleLine` by default, and `theme.other?.playerNameMinWidthMultiLine` when `wrap` is set. (Used the raw inline-style property rather than jest-dom's `toHaveStyle`, since that matcher compares against `getComputedStyle`, which happy-dom resolves `em` units into `px` — `toHaveStyle({minWidth: '18em'})` would never match the computed `'288px'`.)

Note: Storybook's own decorator (`.storybook/preview.tsx`) has the identical bare-`MantineProvider` gap — untouched here since it's outside this diff's scope, but worth knowing if you ever want story-level assertions on `theme.other.*`.

`typecheck`, `lint`, `knip`, and the full `test:components` suite (with coverage) all pass; `PlayerLink.tsx` remains at 100% statements/functions/branches.
